column3: The Hebrew repeats generation and separately says forever; BSB says endless generations to come.
The Hebrew leaves the one angered unnamed; BSB explicitly names the LORD.
The Hebrew has a singular he without naming Moses in the second clause; BSB names Moses.
The Hebrew says they learned the nations’ works; BSB says adopted their customs.
The Hebrew makes them passively humbled under the enemies’ hand; BSB makes the enemies actively subdue them.
The Hebrew names their counsel; BSB says they were bent on rebellion.
The Hebrew first says He saw their distress when hearing the cry; BSB reverses the order.
The Hebrew has plural acts of kindness; BSB says loving devotion.
